Your products and saved items are unchanged. Check ingredient and allergen observations on the product page, or read the current guide.

score.title: Why the TryVit score is retired
score.summary: Food facts and their limitations are more useful than an unsupported overall grade.
score.meaningText: TryVit no longer uses its former weighted aggregate to rank products, declare winners or award health achievements. Historical calculations are retained for audit, not presented as current advice.
score.limitsTitle: What the old number could not establish
score.limitsText: The weights were a project heuristic, not a validated measure of health, safety or personal suitability. Missing inputs could produce a favorable result. General dietary guidance does not validate that formula.
score.actionText: Read the recorded nutrition, its units and measurement basis, ingredients, allergen evidence and sources. Compare only compatible observations. A lower recorded nutrient value is not an overall recommendation.

confidence.title: Understanding product evidence
confidence.summary: Recorded, unknown and unverified are different states—not percentages of correctness.
confidence.meaningText: A recorded field is linked to a retained source observation. It has not necessarily been checked against the package or independently verified. Older catalog values without this lineage remain visibly unverified.
confidence.limitsText: Retrieval time says when TryVit collected information. Source update time says when the source reports a change, not when the package was checked. Completeness counts available fields; it is not a probability that the product information is correct.
confidence.actionText: Missing nutrition is not zero. Missing allergen evidence does not mean allergen-free. Unknown measurement basis prevents a numerical comparison. Check the current package and consult the manufacturer when a consequential detail is unclear.

additives.title: Reading additive information
additives.summary: An ingredient name or additive count is not an individual risk assessment.
additives.meaningText: Food additives serve functions such as preservation, colouring or texture. EFSA assessments consider the substance and dietary exposure; an E number identifies an additive, not a universal danger level.
additives.limitsText: TryVit does not convert the number of additives or its former concern tiers into a health, harm or safety score. A source ingredient list may be incomplete, and combined ingredient evidence is not necessarily the ordered package list.
additives.actionText: Read the actual package, the named additive and the source information. Follow current official guidance for that substance and your circumstances. Missing entries must not be interpreted as proof that an additive is absent.

choices.title: Comparing food information
choices.summary: Use TryVit to inspect evidence and trade-offs, not to choose an overall winner for you.
choices.meaningText: Choose products for the same intended use, then inspect the facts that matter to your shopping task. The wider diet, portion and individual needs are not captured by one product number.
choices.limitsText: Check units, per-100-g versus per-100-ml basis, and as-sold versus prepared values. TryVit withholds numerical comparisons when those are unknown, incompatible or qualified, or when source evidence conflicts.
choices.actionText: Look for missing values, source dates and positive allergen warnings. Check the current package before use. A comparison of recorded quantities is not medical advice or a statement that one product is safer or healthier overall.

dashboard.subtitle: Here's your food overview for today.

tip.0: Whole grains are rich in fibre, B vitamins and minerals. Choose whole-wheat bread over white bread when possible.
tip.1: The WHO recommends less than 5 g of salt per day — roughly one teaspoon. Check sodium on the label.
tip.2: Fruits and vegetables should fill half your plate at every meal for optimal micronutrient intake.
tip.3: Ultra-processed foods (NOVA 4) are linked to higher health risks. Look for NOVA 1–2 alternatives.
tip.4: Drinking water instead of sugary beverages can cut hundreds of empty calories per day.
tip.5: Reading ingredient lists helps spot hidden sugars — look for words ending in '-ose' (glucose, fructose, sucrose).
tip.6: A Nutri-Score of A or B indicates better overall nutritional quality compared to similar products.
tip.7: Saturated fat raises LDL cholesterol. The WHO recommends keeping it below 10% of total energy intake.
tip.8: Dietary fibre supports gut health, lowers cholesterol, and helps regulate blood sugar. Aim for 25–30 g per day.
tip.9: Food additives (E-numbers) aren't all bad, but NOVA 4 products tend to combine many whose long-term effects are still studied.
tip.10: Portion size matters more than you think — even healthy foods add up fast when portions double or triple.
tip.11: Omega-3 fatty acids (ALA, EPA, DHA) support heart and brain health. Look for them in fatty fish, flaxseed, and walnuts.
tip.12: Staying hydrated aids digestion and concentration. Aim for 1.5–2 litres of water daily, more in warm weather.
tip.13: Front-of-pack labels like Nutri-Score summarise nutrition, but always check the full table for a complete picture.

legal.contactIntro: Have questions, feedback, or want to report a data issue? Reach out to us.
legal.responseTime: Private-beta feedback is reviewed in the monitored TryVit issue tracker.
legal.dataWeCollectText: We collect your email address for authentication, your food preferences and allergen settings, and anonymous usage analytics. We do not sell your data or share it with third parties.
legal.howWeUseText: We use account data and saved preferences to support product search, matching against recorded allergen evidence, and access to your saved items. Health-profile records remain available to view or delete; they are not used for personal medical warnings, health scores or current nutrition advice.
legal.dataStorageText: All data is stored on Supabase (PostgreSQL) hosted in the EU. We use row-level security to ensure you can only access your own data.
legal.yourRightsText: Under GDPR, you have the right to access, correct, or delete your personal data. Contact us at the email below to exercise these rights.
legal.acceptanceText: By using TryVit, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.
legal.serviceDescText: TryVit provides food product information, health scores, and nutritional data sourced from Open Food Facts and our own analysis. This is for informational purposes only and does not constitute medical or dietary advice.
legal.dataAccuracyText: While we strive for accuracy, food data may contain errors. Always check product labels for allergen and nutritional information. We are not liable for decisions made based on our data.
legal.userAccountsText: You are responsible for maintaining the security of your account. Do not share your credentials. We reserve the right to suspend accounts that violate these terms.
legal.liabilityText: TryVit is provided "as is" without warranties. We are not liable for any damages arising from the use of this service.
legal.imageWhatWeProcessText: Barcode images (camera-based barcode scanning) and product label images (OCR text extraction — Beta feature, coming soon).
legal.imageOnDevice: All image processing happens entirely on your device (in your browser)
legal.imageNeverUploaded: Images are NEVER uploaded to our servers
legal.imageNotStored: Images are processed in temporary memory and immediately discarded after use
legal.imageOnlyText: Only extracted text (barcode numbers or label text) is used for product search
legal.imageCameraText: Camera access requires your explicit permission. You can revoke it at any time in your browser settings. The camera feed is only active while you are using the scanning feature.
legal.imageDataCollectedText: We collect barcode numbers (EAN codes) extracted from barcode scans and, in the future, extracted text strings from OCR processing. We do NOT collect the images themselves.
legal.imageLegalBasisText: Consent (GDPR Article 6(1)(a)) — you choose to use the camera feature. Legitimate interest (GDPR Article 6(1)(f)) — providing product lookup functionality.
legal.contactText: For questions about these terms, contact us at:

nutriScore.A: Nutri-Score A: Best nutritional quality. Low in fat, sugar, and salt. High in fiber, protein, and fruits/vegetables.
nutriScore.B: Nutri-Score B: Good nutritional quality. Slightly higher in some nutrients than A, but still a healthy choice.
nutriScore.C: Nutri-Score C: Average nutritional quality. Moderate levels of fat, sugar, or salt. Consume in reasonable amounts.
nutriScore.D: Nutri-Score D: Below average nutritional quality. Higher in fat, sugar, or salt. Choose less frequently.
nutriScore.E: Nutri-Score E: Lowest nutritional quality. High in fat, sugar, and/or salt. Consume sparingly.
nutriScore.unknown: Nutri-Score not available. Insufficient data to compute the score for this product.

nova.1: NOVA 1: Unprocessed or minimally processed food. Examples: fresh fruits, vegetables, grains, plain meat, eggs.
nova.2: NOVA 2: Processed culinary ingredient. Used in food preparation. Examples: oils, butter, sugar, salt, flour.
nova.3: NOVA 3: Processed food. Made by combining NOVA 1 & 2. Examples: canned vegetables, cheese, bread, cured meats.
nova.4: NOVA 4: Ultra-processed product. Industrial formulations with additives. Examples: soft drinks, packaged snacks, instant noodles.

score.green: Score 1–20 (Green): Low health risk. This product has favorable nutritional composition.
score.yellow: Score 21–40 (Yellow): Moderate health risk. Some nutritional concerns but generally acceptable.
score.orange: Score 41–60 (Orange): Elevated health risk. Notable levels of unhealthy nutrients or additives.
score.red: Score 61–80 (Red): High health risk. Significant amounts of fat, sugar, salt, or concerning additives.
score.darkred: Score 81–100 (Dark Red): Very high health risk. Multiple unhealthy factors at high levels.

confidence.high: High confidence: Most data fields verified. Nutrition, ingredients, allergens, and source information are complete and cross-validated.
confidence.medium: Medium confidence: Key data present but some fields estimated or incomplete. Scores are reliable but may shift with better data.
confidence.low: Low confidence: Significant data gaps. Score may not reflect true product quality. We're working to improve coverage.

concern.0: EFSA Concern Level 0: No known safety concerns. This additive is well-studied and considered safe at typical dietary levels.
concern.1: EFSA Concern Level 1 (Low): Minimal safety considerations. Widely used, generally safe, but some studies suggest monitoring at very high intake.
concern.2: EFSA Concern Level 2 (Moderate): Some safety considerations. EFSA has noted potential effects at high doses. Used in many processed foods.
concern.3: EFSA Concern Level 3 (High): Significant safety considerations. EFSA recommends intake limits. Some countries restrict use in certain food categories.

nutriScore.title: Understanding Nutri-Score
nutriScore.description: What the A–E grades mean and how they're calculated.
nutriScore.summary: Nutri-Score compares nutritional profiles from A to E. It is not a safety assessment or a recommendation for an individual.
nutriScore.whatIsText: Nutri-Score is a voluntary front-of-pack label developed by Santé publique France and used in several European countries. It summarizes nutritional composition per 100 g or 100 ml; it is not mandatory throughout the EU.
nutriScore.howItWorksText: The calculation balances energy, sugars, saturated fat and salt against components such as fibre, protein, fruit, vegetables and legumes. Rules and thresholds depend on the food category and algorithm version; beverages have specific rules. France introduced the updated algorithm in 2025.
nutriScore.negativeLabel: Components that increase the numerical score
nutriScore.positiveLabel: Components that can reduce the numerical score
nutriScore.gradeA: A — Most favourable profile on this scale
nutriScore.gradeE: E — Least favourable profile on this scale
nutriScore.limitationsText: A grade does not describe the whole diet, the portion you eat, allergens or individual suitability. It is not a processing classification or an additive safety assessment. Grades from different algorithm versions may differ.
nutriScore.unknownText: UNKNOWN means no usable grade is available in the record. NOT-APPLICABLE is a separate recorded state. Neither is a favourable grade, and missing information alone does not establish why a grade is absent.
nutriScore.ourApproachText: TryVit presents the recorded grade alongside nutrition and ingredient information. A source grade does not establish which algorithm version was used unless that version is documented. Unknown provenance or version remains unknown.

novaGroups.title: NOVA Food Classification
novaGroups.description: Understanding food processing levels from minimally processed to ultra-processed.
novaGroups.summary: NOVA groups foods by the nature, extent and purpose of processing. The four groups do not measure the health risk of an individual product.
novaGroups.whatIsText: NOVA is a food classification system developed by researchers at the University of São Paulo. Unlike Nutri-Score, which focuses on nutrients, NOVA focuses on the degree and purpose of food processing.
novaGroups.group1Text: Unprocessed foods or foods changed by processes such as drying, milling, freezing or pasteurization without adding salt, sugar or oil. Examples include fruit, plain milk and plain flour.
novaGroups.group2Text: Ingredients obtained from foods or nature for preparing meals, such as oil, butter, sugar and salt.
novaGroups.group3Text: Foods made by adding culinary ingredients to minimally processed foods, such as vegetables preserved in brine or bread made from flour, water, yeast and salt. The actual formulation matters.
novaGroups.group4Text: Industrial formulations characterized by substances rarely used in kitchens or additives serving functions such as flavouring or colouring. Ingredient count alone does not define this group.
novaGroups.whyItMattersText: NOVA describes a different aspect of food from nutrient composition. Studies of dietary patterns cannot assign a personal health risk to a single product or prove that every product in a group has the same effects.
novaGroups.polishContextText: Products sold by the same shop can belong to different NOVA groups. Check the particular formulation and available evidence; the retailer, packaging and ingredient count do not determine the group.
novaGroups.processingRiskText: TryVit can show a recorded NOVA group as processing information. It is not converted into a low, moderate or high health-risk verdict. Missing or uncertain classification remains unresolved.

allergens.title: Allergens in Food
allergens.description: EU mandatory allergens, Polish label reading, and 'contains' vs 'may contain'.
allergens.summary: EU rules identify 14 categories of substances or products causing allergies or intolerances. A missing warning in TryVit does not establish that a food is allergen-free.
allergens.eu14Text: Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 requires declaration of relevant ingredients and processing aids listed in Annex II that remain in the food. They are generally emphasized in the ingredients list. Specific derivatives are exempt; this is a summary, not the full legal list.
allergens.allergen1: Cereals containing gluten (including wheat, spelt, khorasan wheat, rye, barley, oats and their hybridised strains)
allergens.allergen8: Tree nuts (almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts, cashews, pecans, Brazil nuts, pistachios, macadamias)
allergens.allergen12: Sulphur dioxide and sulphites (>10 mg/kg or >10 mg/l, as total SO₂ in the food ready for consumption)
allergens.containsVsTracesText: 'Contains' declares an allergen in the food. 'May contain' is a precautionary warning about possible unintended presence. Neither the absence of that warning nor an empty database field proves absence of an allergen.
allergens.polishLabelsText: Allergen names must stand out in an ingredients list, for example through bold type or UPPERCASE. 'Zawiera' means 'contains'. Common terms include mleko (milk), jaja (eggs), pszenica (wheat), soja (soybeans), orzechy (nuts), sezam (sesame), seler (celery) and gorczyca (mustard).
allergens.inTryVitText: TryVit displays available recorded allergen information; this does not establish independent verification of the current package. Check the actual label and contact the manufacturer if information is missing or unclear.

readingLabels.title: Reading Polish Food Labels
readingLabels.description: How to interpret nutrition tables, units, portions and common label elements.
readingLabels.summary: Polish food labels follow EU regulations and contain standardized nutritional information. Learning to read them helps you compare products fairly and make informed choices.
readingLabels.nutritionTableText: Most prepacked foods require a nutrition declaration, with exemptions including foods listed in Annex V of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011. The standard declaration covers energy, fat, saturates, carbohydrate, sugars, protein and salt per 100 g or 100 ml.
readingLabels.per100gTitle: Per 100 g or 100 ml and per portion
readingLabels.per100gText: Compare similar products on the same basis: per 100 g or per 100 ml, and as sold or as prepared. Portion information may also be supplied. Check its stated size and how it relates to the amount you eat.
readingLabels.mandatoryTitle: Common label elements (requirements and exemptions vary)
readingLabels.mandatoryItem2: Ingredients (skład) — generally listed by weight at the time of use, with exceptions
readingLabels.mandatoryItem3: Relevant allergens — emphasized in the ingredients list
readingLabels.mandatoryItem5: Best before / Use by date (najlepiej spożyć przed / należy spożyć do)
readingLabels.mandatoryItem6: Special storage conditions or conditions of use, where needed
readingLabels.mandatoryItem7: Name and address of the responsible food business operator
readingLabels.mandatoryItem9: Nutrition declaration (wartość odżywcza), subject to exemptions
readingLabels.tip1: Match units and preparation state before comparing nutrient values.
readingLabels.tip2: Read what the ingredients are; list length alone does not determine processing or nutritional quality.
readingLabels.tip3: Earlier ingredients generally weigh more individually, but the first three need not form a majority.
readingLabels.tip4: Glucose-fructose syrup (syrop glukozowo-fruktozowy) and dextrose (dekstroza) supply sugars. Maltodextrin is not equivalent to 'sugars' in the nutrition declaration.
readingLabels.tip5: The EAN barcode (kod kreskowy) is the product's unique identifier used in our database.

overnight-oats.title: Overnight Oats with Yogurt & Berries
overnight-oats.description: Creamy overnight oats with optional fresh berries.

steps.1: Combine oats, yogurt, and milk in a jar. Stir well.
steps.2: Cover and refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours).
steps.3: Top with fresh berries, if using, before serving.

jajecznica.title: Polish Scrambled Eggs (Jajecznica)
jajecznica.description: Classic Polish-style scrambled eggs with butter and chives.

steps.1: Melt butter in a non-stick pan over low heat.
steps.2: Crack eggs into the pan and stir gently with a spatula.
steps.3: Cook slowly until just set but still creamy. Season and serve with chives.

zupa-pomidorowa.title: Tomato Soup (Zupa Pomidorowa)
zupa-pomidorowa.description: Traditional Polish tomato soup served with noodles or rice.

steps.1: Sauté diced onion in butter until soft.
steps.2: Add crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Simmer 15 minutes.
steps.3: Blend until smooth, season with salt and sugar.
steps.4: Serve with cooked pasta or rice.

chicken-salad-yogurt.title: Chicken Salad with Yogurt Dressing
chicken-salad-yogurt.description: Light chicken salad with a creamy yogurt-herb dressing.

steps.1: Grill or poach chicken breast and slice thinly.
steps.2: Toss mixed greens, cucumber, and tomatoes in a bowl.
steps.3: Mix yogurt with lemon juice, garlic, and herbs for dressing.
steps.4: Top salad with chicken slices and drizzle dressing.

baked-salmon-vegetables.title: Baked Salmon with Roasted Vegetables
baked-salmon-vegetables.description: Oven-baked salmon fillet with seasonal roasted vegetables.

steps.1: Preheat oven to 200°C. Season salmon with olive oil, lemon, and herbs.
steps.2: Toss vegetables with olive oil and spread on a baking sheet.
steps.3: Place salmon on the sheet and bake for 20 minutes.

ingredients.2: 1 cup mixed vegetables (zucchini, bell pepper, onion)

pierogi-simplified.title: Simple Potato & Cheese Pierogi
pierogi-simplified.description: Simplified pierogi with a potato and farmer's cheese filling.

steps.1: Make dough: mix flour, egg, water and a pinch of salt. Knead until smooth.
steps.2: Prepare filling: mash boiled potatoes with farmer's cheese and season.
steps.3: Roll dough, cut circles, fill and pinch edges to seal.
steps.4: Boil pierogi until they float. Serve with caramelized onions.
steps.5: Optionally pan-fry boiled pierogi in butter until golden.

yogurt-nuts-honey.title: Greek Yogurt with Nuts & Honey
yogurt-nuts-honey.description: Quick, protein-rich snack with crunchy nuts and sweet honey.

steps.2: Top with mixed nuts and a drizzle of honey.

hummus-vegetables.title: Hummus with Fresh Vegetables
hummus-vegetables.description: Creamy hummus served with colorful vegetable sticks.

steps.1: Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and olive oil until smooth.
steps.3: Serve hummus with vegetable sticks for dipping.

ingredients.4: Carrot, cucumber, and bell pepper sticks

red-lentil-soup.title: Red Lentil Soup
red-lentil-soup.description: Hearty and warming red lentil soup with cumin and lemon.

steps.1: Sauté onion, carrot, and garlic in olive oil.
steps.2: Add lentils, cumin, and broth. Bring to a boil.
steps.3: Simmer 20 minutes until lentils are soft.
steps.4: Blend partially, season with lemon juice and salt.

mediterranean-quinoa-salad.title: Mediterranean Quinoa Salad
mediterranean-quinoa-salad.description: Fresh quinoa salad with cherry tomatoes, olives, and feta.

steps.1: Cook quinoa according to package directions and cool.
steps.3: Toss quinoa with vegetables, crumbled feta, olive oil, and lemon juice.

green-smoothie.title: Green Smoothie
green-smoothie.description: Nutrient-packed green smoothie with spinach and banana.

steps.1: Add all ingredients to a blender.
steps.2: Blend on high until smooth. Add more liquid if needed.
steps.3: Pour into a glass and serve immediately.

ingredients.3: ½ cup milk or plant-based alternative

baked-apples-cinnamon.title: Baked Apples with Cinnamon
baked-apples-cinnamon.description: Warm baked apples with a cinnamon-oat crumble topping.

steps.1: Preheat oven to 180°C. Core apples and place in a baking dish.
steps.2: Mix oats, cinnamon, honey, and a little butter for the filling.
steps.3: Stuff apples with the mixture and bake 25 minutes.
steps.4: Serve warm, optionally with a spoonful of yogurt.
